brief_data.deck: Lime launched its IPO roadshow on 22 June: 6.96M shares at $24-$26, up to about $181M at a valuation of up to about $1.8B (Renaissance Capital), Nasdaq ticker LIME. A profitable, electric, city-centre mobility brand is about to become public in the cities where Formula E races.

risks.label: A SCOOTER BRAND IN A B2B PADDOCK
risks.detail: Lime is a consumer brand with thin margins after debt; a sponsorship line competes with city-licence costs and fleet capex.
risks.counter: Size the entry at the low end and weight it to in-kind fleet and ride credits, which cost Lime little.

risks.label: LISTING FIRST, BRAND SECOND
risks.detail: Pricing and the quiet period come before any marketing decision; the window may not open until the first public quarter.
risks.counter: Approach after pricing with a London-finale package that needs only a July decision.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Wayne Ting in the week after pricing to agree a London E-Prix activation for 15-16 August and size a three-season Official Micromobility Partner entry with Envision Racing for the GEN4 era.

value.text: Lime rider zones and ticket-holder ride credits at the London, Berlin and Madrid E-Prix; Envision-liveried e-bikes in each host city during race week; push and in-app messaging to riders in those cities. The team gets a city-wide presence for a city race.
value.label: Race-week mechanics (Mode B)

value.text: Envision's partners are industrial and enterprise brands. Lime brings a consumer audience across about 230 cities and the Uber ecosystem behind its largest shareholder, which is reach the team cannot buy at this price elsewhere.
value.label: Audience the roster lacks

value.text: Driver and team commutes on Lime, a season-long 'last mile to the grid' series, and a shared climate-impact scoreboard built from Lime's ride data and the team's Race Against Climate Change reporting.
value.label: Content

value.text: Official Micromobility Partner designation, car and race-suit placement, host-city activation rights, hospitality at London and Berlin, and a public-company partner announcement timed to the GEN4 launch in December.
value.label: What Envision gives back

why_now.text: On 22 June 2026 Lime announced the launch of its IPO roadshow: 6,956,522 shares (6,679,791 from Lime, 276,731 from selling stockholders) at $24-$26, listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as LIME, with Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan leading. Renaissance Capital sized the deal at up to $181M and a valuation of up to $1.8B; pricing was expected the following week.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: FY2025 revenue was $886.7M, up 29%, adjusted EBITDA $218.1M, operating income $70.4M and free cash flow $103.8M, the third positive year. The $59.3M net loss is a debt-cost story: proceeds repay a $115M term loan at 10% due September 2026. After the listing Lime's cash flow is its own.
why_now.label: The business behind the listing

why_now.text: Uber, Lime's largest holder at 24.4%, has indicated interest in up to $20M of shares. A newly public consumer brand has to explain to investors and city governments why it belongs in the centre of cities. Formula E's street circuits in London, Berlin, Madrid, Miami and Austin are that argument on television.
why_now.label: A public brand needs a public story

why_now.text: The IPO priced on 30 June 2026 at $25, the mid-point, and trading began on 1 July; TechCrunch reported $167M raised at an implied valuation of about $1.66B (about $174M including selling stockholders). The London E-Prix on 15-16 August remains the first activation window; Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18-19 December.
why_now.label: Update since issue

why_team.text: Envision Racing's roster is Envision Group (title), Sand Technologies, Teijin and Genpact. No Formula E team carries a shared-mobility, e-bike or e-scooter partner, so Official Micromobility Partner is a first-of-category designation at a team-partner price.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Envision Racing built its brand on the Race Against Climate Change programme; Lime's pitch to cities is car-trip replacement. The two stories are the same story, told to fans and to city halls.
why_team.label: Climate identity

why_team.text: Six Formula E teams are owned by car makers or two-wheel makers (Jaguar, Nissan, Porsche, Cupra, Citroën, Mahindra, and Yamaha in the Lola entry). An independent team can put a scooter brand on the car without an OEM marketing department objecting.
why_team.label: Independent, not a works team

why_team.text: Envision is British-based and the London E-Prix is its home race. Lime has served more than 400,000 London customers and runs both e-bikes and e-scooters there. A finale activation in August needs only a July decision.
why_team.label: London is home for both

ruled_out.team: Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team
ruled_out.reason: Yamaha, a title partner, makes e-bikes and scooters: direct category conflict.

ruled_out.team: Jaguar TCS Racing · Nissan Formula E Team · Porsche Formula E Team · Cupra Kiro · Citroën Racing
ruled_out.reason: OEM works entries; mobility messaging stays with the car maker.
Mahindra & Mahindra builds vehicles, including electric two- and three-wheelers; category conflict.
DS has announced its exit at the end of the season; entry future unresolved.
Open and US-based, a credible second choice, but Lime's revenue centre and the finale are in Europe and Envision offers the climate identity and London home race.

brief_data.bottom_line: A profitable electric mobility brand listing on Nasdaq this month, an open micromobility lane on every Formula E roster, and a season finale in its biggest European market eight weeks out. Envision Racing is the clean, independent, climate-led home; the deal is small, in-kind heavy and time-bound.

score_cells.note: Electric, urban, consumer: FE's cities are Lime's.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Lime announced the roadshow on 22 June with pricing expected the following week; Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan lead the books and Uber, holder of 24.4% pre-IPO, has indicated interest in up to $20M of shares. The business on sale is no longer a scooter story: FY2025 revenue was $886.7M, up 29%, with adjusted EBITDA of $218.1M and free cash flow of $103.8M, a third positive year, against a $59.3M net loss driven by debt costs. Proceeds repay a $115M term loan at 10% due in September 2026, which frees the cash flow behind it.
brief_data.the_case_p2: A newly listed consumer brand needs a public-market story about scale and cities, and Formula E races in Lime's cities. London, where Lime has served more than 400,000 customers, hosts the season finale on 15-16 August; Berlin and Madrid follow in the GEN4 season. No shared-mobility brand has ever raced on the grid, so the first one defines the category.

brief_data.industry_meta: Shared Electric Micromobility · E-bikes and E-scooters
brief_data.value_content: MODE B - halo with hard mechanics. Lime-liveried rider zones and ride credits for ticket holders at the London, Berlin and Madrid E-Prix, team-branded e-bikes in each host city during race week, and a rider-app audience in the tens of millions for Envision's climate content. For the team: a consumer brand that turns a city race into a city-wide campaign, and Uber-backed distribution the roster does not yet have.
brief_data.why_team_para: Envision Racing carries Envision Group as title partner with Sand Technologies, Teijin and Genpact alongside; there is no mobility or consumer-transport partner, so the lane is clean. The team is British-based and built its identity on the Race Against Climate Change, the same car-replacement argument Lime makes to city halls. It is an independent, not an OEM works entry, so a two-wheel brand is a fit rather than a conflict. London is its home race and Lime's largest European market.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Micromobility Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, the whole first GEN4 cycle. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year plus in-kind fleet and ride credits. Scope: car and suit placement, host-city activation in Lime cities, app and rider communications, hospitality at London and Berlin.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Pricing lands next week and the first public-company brand budget is set in July, with the London E-Prix on 15-16 August eight weeks out. Season 13 opens in Jeddah in December with a GEN4 car and a 21-race calendar.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Ting has run Lime since May 2020, joining in 2018 after four years at Uber including Chief of Staff to its CEO. Path: Joseph Kraus, President; Ann Gugino, CFO since December 2023; Hannah McClellan Richards, COO from June 2026. No chief marketing officer is listed among the executive officers.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Wayne, you are about to list a brand that lives in London, Berlin and Madrid, and Formula E races in all three. No mobility brand has ever been on that grid. 25 minutes after pricing to see how Envision would put Lime in the finale?”
